title: Transport of cohomology along the geometric Frobenius
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen
algebraic closure $\Qlb$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated
finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k_0$-scheme, put
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\Spec k$, and let $a_Y:Y\to s$ be the structure
morphism, so that $Y$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Let
$\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$ and
$g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma):Y\to Y$ be the geometric
Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and put $g_s=\Spec(\gamma):s\to s$.
Then $a_Y\circ g_Y=g_s\circ a_Y$, and, since $g_Y$ and $g_s$ are
isomorphisms, the commutative square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
 Y & \xrightarrow{\ g_Y\ } & Y\\
 a_Y\downarrow & & \downarrow a_Y\\
 s & \xrightarrow{\ g_s\ } & s
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian, with the identification
$(g_Y,a_Y):Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_{s,g_s}s$; it is called the
*Frobenius square* of $Y_0$. Use the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the derived pullback
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the derived direct image
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], the compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], the point fiber functor
$\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and the
cohomology complexes $\RGamma(Y,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}(-))$ and
$\RGammac(Y,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}(-))$
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. For $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ define
the following maps.

1. *Exchange along the Frobenius square.* The direct-image exchange

$$
 \operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M):
 Lg_s^*Ra_{Y*}M\longrightarrow Ra_{Y*}Lg_Y^*M
$$

is the exchange transformation $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ of the Frobenius square
[def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]: the mate, under
$La_Y^*\dashv Ra_{Y*}$, of the composite
$La_Y^*Lg_s^*Ra_{Y*}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_Y^*La_Y^*Ra_{Y*}M
\xrightarrow{Lg_Y^*(\varepsilon_M)}Lg_Y^*M$, where $\varepsilon$ is the
counit of $La_Y^*\dashv Ra_{Y*}$. It is formed at a finite coefficient level
and passed to $\Lambda$ by the compatible finite reductions, the derived
inverse limit, the rationalization and the common-stage construction, as the
operations $Lg^*$ and $Ra_*$ themselves are. The compact-support exchange

$$
 \operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M):
 Lg_s^*Ra_{Y!}M\longrightarrow Ra_{Y!}Lg_Y^*M
$$

is the compact-support exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of
[def-exchange-projection], formed by its recipe for the Frobenius square:
choose a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]
$Y_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline Y_0\xrightarrow{p_0}\Spec k_0$ of the
structure morphism of $Y_0$, let
$Y\xrightarrow{j}\overline Y\xrightarrow{p}s$ be its base change to $k$,
which is a compactification of $a_Y$ and computes $Ra_{Y!}=Rp_*j_!$, and put
$g_{\overline Y}=\operatorname{id}_{\overline Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma)$, so that
$p\,g_{\overline Y}=g_s\,p$ and $g_{\overline Y}\,j=j\,g_Y$, both squares
being Cartesian for the same reason as the Frobenius square. Then
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M)$ is the composite

$$
 Lg_s^*Rp_*j_!M\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Ex}_*\ }
 Rp_*Lg_{\overline Y}^*j_!M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 Rp_*j_!Lg_Y^*M
$$

of the direct-image exchange of the square $(p,g_{\overline Y},g_s)$ and the
canonical identification $Lg_{\overline Y}^*j_!\cong j_!Lg_Y^*$ of extension
by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] along the open square
$(j,g_{\overline Y},g_Y)$, as in [def-exchange-projection]; its independence
of the chosen compactification is part of the compactification coherence
[prop-compactification-coherence-detailed].

2. *Point transport.* For $N\in D^b_c(s,\Lambda)$ the map

$$
 \iota_N:\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N)
$$

is defined at a finite coefficient level as follows. $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is
evaluation at the geometric point $\operatorname{id}:s\to s$ of
$s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Since $g_s$ is an isomorphism, the inverse image is
given on sections by $(g_s^{-1}N)(U\xrightarrow{u}s)=N(U\xrightarrow{g_su}s)$,
the pair $(U\xrightarrow{g_su}s,\ \operatorname{id}_U)$ being initial among
the pairs $(V\to s,\ U\to V\times_{s,g_s}s)$ indexing the colimit that defines
$g_s^{-1}N(U)$, and $Lg_s^*N=g_s^{-1}N$ because $g_s^{-1}\Lambda_s=\Lambda_s$;
hence $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N)=N(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)$, and $\iota_N$ is
the restriction map of $N$ along the isomorphism
$g_s:(s\xrightarrow{g_s}s)\to(s\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}s)$ of
$s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$ it is obtained from
the finite-level maps by the derived inverse limit, the rationalization and
the common-stage construction, as $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ itself is.

3. *Transport of cohomology along $g_Y$.* The transport of ordinary
cohomology is the composite

$$
 \tau_M:\RGamma(Y,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}M)
 \xrightarrow{\ \iota_{Ra_{Y*}M}\ }
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*Ra_{Y*}M)
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,*}(M))\ }
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y*}Lg_Y^*M)=\RGamma(Y,Lg_Y^*M),
$$

and the transport of compactly supported cohomology is the composite

$$
 \tau_{c,M}:\RGammac(Y,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}M)
 \xrightarrow{\ \iota_{Ra_{Y!}M}\ }
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*Ra_{Y!}M)
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Fib}_s(\operatorname{FrEx}_{Y,!}(M))\ }
 \operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Y!}Lg_Y^*M)=\RGammac(Y,Lg_Y^*M).
$$

Both are natural in $M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, being composites of natural
transformations. For every integer $i$, $\mathrm H^i(\tau_M):H^i(Y,M)\to
H^i(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$ and $\mathrm H^i(\tau_{c,M}):H_c^i(Y,M)\to H_c^i(Y,Lg_Y^*M)$
are the induced maps on cohomology groups.

mathlib_searches.results: AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/ElladicCohomology.lean (defines Scheme.ellAdicSheaf and Scheme.EllAdicCohomology: the pro-etale cohomology groups H^i(X, Z_l) of a scheme, no functoriality in X, no Frobenius, no compact supports, no derived direct image) and AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/BigZariski.lean (docstring mention only)

nothing in AlgebraicGeometry/; elsewhere only the ring-theoretic Frobenius (RingTheory/Frobenius.lean, Algebra/CharP/Frobenius.lean, WittVector/Frobenius.lean, FieldTheory/Perfect.lean): the q-power map of a ring, no scheme morphism Y -> Y and no action on cohomology

CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean (mates of squares of adjunctions, the abstract form of an exchange map); CategoryTheory/Sites/Pullback.lean (sheafPullback, sheafAdjunctionContinuous: the underived pullback-pushforward adjunction for a continuous functor of sites); Sites/SheafCohomology/Basic.lean (Sheaf.H F n as Ext from the constant sheaf); Sites/Point/* (points of sites and fiber functors). No derived direct image Rf_*, no Rf_!, no exchange transformation for a square of schemes, no transport of cohomology along an automorphism
